To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of a discrete change in intrinsic membrane current on the action potentials of the surrounding cells are markedly different for alterations that affect the plateau or pacemaker currents vs the rising phase currents, that these effects are dependent on the site of stimulation, and that the spatial pattern of cell-to-cell coupling resistances also affects the spatial distribution of altered action potential parameters.

the spatial distribution of changes in action potential properties resulting in a discrete region with a localized alteration in membrane properties depends on the site of stimulation, the underlying pattern of cell-cell electrical coupling, and the intrinsic membrane currents that are altered in the discrete region.

the effects of regional changes in intrinsic membrane properties are spatially heterogeneous, that this heterogeneity depends on the specific membrane current affected, the site of stimulation, and the underlying distribution of cell-cell coupling resistances, and that the resulting effects on the spatial distribution of the action potential parameters are not predictable from the effects observed in a single cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of changes in intrinsic membrane properties on the spatial distribution of the action potential in a cardiac syncytium, and with the effects of the spatial distribution of these changes on the resulting spatial distribution of action potentials.
the effects of regional alterations of membrane properties of the heart on action potential propagation and the resulting spatial patterns of action potential properties.

understanding the effects of discrete regional changes in membrane properties on the propagation of action potentials in the heart, with the goal of developing a better understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of arrhythmias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spatial distribution of any parameter measured from a single-cell penetration in an electrical tissue is determined not only by the intrinsic properties of that cell, but also by the spatial pattern of the underlying electrotonic interactions between the cell and its neighbors.

a regional change in intrinsic cardiac membrane properties will result in a spatially heterogeneous distribution of action potential characteristics, and that the resulting spatial pattern is a complex function of the site of stimulation, the site of the regional change in intrinsic properties, and the underlying spatial distribution of cell-cell coupling resistances.

the spatial pattern of action potential parameters is determined by the interplay between the intrinsic membrane properties, the pattern of coupling resistance, the site of stimulation, and the underlying spatial distribution of membrane currents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the action potential properties of the heart reflect the combined effects of intrinsic membrane properties, the spatial distribution of cell-cell coupling, and the site of stimulation.

a discrete change in membrane properties in a region of the heart can have very different consequences on the spatial distribution of the resulting action potential properties depending upon the type of current that is altered, and that these consequences can be further modified by the site of stimulation.
the action potential properties measured from a single site in an electrically coupled cell population do not provide a complete description of that population's intrinsic properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial pattern of action potential properties in the heart reflects the combined effects of intrinsic membrane properties and the spatial pattern of electrotonic interactions.

, in order to understand the functional consequences of a regional change in intrinsic properties in an electrically coupled system such as the heart, it is necessary to consider the effects of both the intrinsic properties of the cell and the spatial pattern of cell to cell coupling.

a localized change in the intrinsic membrane property of a small number of cells in a syncytium can have a profound impact on the action potential properties in a much larger area of the tissue, and that the spatial distribution of the effects of such a localized change is highly dependent on the specific membrane current affected and the site of stimulation.
